_doc: The weekly scout report: what exists out there that this box is not using. Written by the Claude routine described in docs/models.md and read by src/lib/model-scout.ts. Judgment lives here; facts about which model ids a vendor currently sells are NOT — those are pulled live from each vendor's model-list endpoint at read time, because a list committed to git is out of date the day after it is written. Fit verdicts are likewise computed at read time and never stored here: a verdict depends on what is running and how much disk is free, and both change hourly. They are now computed PER HOST — measured against the machine this console is running on, and against each other host's declared specs in config/hosts/*.json — so a claim in `why` or `notes` that a model does not fit needs to name which machine it means.
_schema: candidates[]: { id, name, kind: local|cloud, capability, why, checkpoint?, provider?, target?, mode?, params?, released?, license?, docs?, paper?, requirement? { vramGb, ramGb, diskGb, basis, estimated }, spec? { paramsB, precision, contextK, kind }, runtimes?, pricing? }. Give `requirement` when the authors published usable numbers; give `spec` otherwise and let estimateFromParams() do the arithmetic with an honest basis string. `runtimes` pins weights to one stack (e.g. ["metal"] for an MLX repo) and MUST be omitted for portable weights, which is most of them — absent means "runs anywhere", and GGUF counts as portable. Verdicts are computed per HOST: name which machine you mean in `why` and `notes`, because BeTenshi (31.8 GB VRAM + 63 GB host RAM) and B5 (one 128 GB unified pool) disagree about a good number of models. upgrades[]: { alias, from, to, why } — a like-for-like repoint of an alias already in ai-router.yaml.
generatedBy: weekly scout, 2026-11-02 — ON SCHEDULE: the last report is dated 2026-10-26 and the schedule is 47 5 * * 1 UTC, so this is a 7-day gap on a 7-day schedule, the first clean interval since August. THE WEEK'S BIGGEST FINDING IS IN notes, NOT candidates: nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B is now the open #1 ASR model on English short-form, long-form AND multilingual simultaneously, and it is held out on three separate counts — see note 2. candidates.name: LTX-2.5 22B IC-LoRA Pixel Spatial Upscaler
candidates.params: an adapter, not a model: 329 MB of LoRA weights over the 22B LTX-2.5 DiT already installed
candidates.license: other (ltx-2.x-community-license), gated: auto — AND THIS IS THE SAME LICENCE AS THE LTX-2.5 ALREADY INSTALLED AND SERVING ON BETENSHI, which is where the licence argument in `why` comes from

requirement.basis: THESE NUMBERS ARE THE MARGINAL COST OF AN ADAPTER, NOT THE COST OF RUNNING IT, and the distinction has to be read before the verdict is. Disk is EXACT from the repo listing read 02-11: usedStorage 329,292,979 B for the whole repo, one diffusion-single-file LoRA. VRAM is that x 1.15, which is what the adapter adds on top of a DiT that is already resident. THE REAL CONSTRAINT IS THE BASE: this LoRA does nothing without local-ltx-2.5, which config/model-meta.json declares at 16 GB VRAM / 38 GB host RAM as an ADMISSION figure, and which docs/video-forge.md measured at a 28.4 GB whole-card peak in the 02-10 bake-off. So the console's fit check will call this entry trivially fittable and it is right to: the question 'can BeTenshi run LTX-2.5' was already answered yes on 02-10. Nothing here is measured on this box, and no quality figure is claimed — see `why`.

candidates.why: THE CHEAPEST THING ON THIS LIST TO FIND OUT ABOUT, AND THE FIRST ENTRY THE `upscale` LANE HAS EVER HAD (docs/models.md records that lane as 'nothing' on 01-11). WHAT IT WOULD REPLACE, with a measured number: the Video Forge upscales one film in four with Real-ESRGAN x2, and the 02-10 bake-off timed that at 1103 s for 14 clips — about 80 s a clip, so roughly 2.4 hours on a 108-clip film, inside a 01:00-07:00 window. This is a 329 MB in-context LoRA that does spatial upscaling inside the DiT that generated the clip, on weights ComfyUI already has loaded, so the comparison is 'another pass over the same latents' against 'a separate classical upscaler at 80 s a clip'. THE LICENCE ARGUMENT, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS THE ONLY REASON THIS IS A CANDIDATE RATHER THAN A NOTE: the repo is `license: other` (ltx-2.x-community-license) and `gated: auto`, which docs/models.md normally holds in `notes` as unread terms. It is listed anyway because these are NOT NEW TERMS TO THIS BOX — Lightricks/LTX-2.5 itself is `gated: auto` under ltx-2.x-community-license-agreement, somebody already clicked through it, and local-ltx-2.5 is in config/model-meta.json and served by the comfyui service on :8188 in config/hosts/betenshi.json. If that reading is wrong — if the base was obtained some other way, or the adapter's terms differ from the base's — this drops to a note and nothing else in the report changes. THE REAL RISK IS TECHNICAL, NOT LEGAL, and it is worth saying before the download: model-meta records local-ltx-2.5 as an 18.7 GB NVFP4 DiT, and whether a bf16 IC-LoRA applies cleanly to an NVFP4-quantised base in ComfyUI is NOT KNOWN HERE. That is the thing to test, and the cost of testing it is 329 MB. NO QUALITY NUMBER IS CLAIMED: there is no public video-upscaling board, Lightricks publishes no PSNR or LPIPS for this adapter, and nobody has put it beside Real-ESRGAN on this box. 13,161 downloads in the last 30 days and 24,797 all-time (metric stated per docs/models.md), and four community Spaces run it. THIS IS A BETENSHI ENTRY ONLY: B5 has no ComfyUI — its video path is local-draw-things-wan-video through Draw Things — so an LTX IC-LoRA has nothing to attach to there, and that is a stack fact, not a size one. The sibling Lightricks/LTX-2.3-22b-IC-LoRA-Pixel-Spatial-Upscaler exists for the older base and is not wanted; 2.5 is what is installed.

candidates.name: LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.5 (audio-driven talking video, 8-step DMD2)
candidates.params: 15.85B in the avatar DiT (31.71 GB of bf16 shards / 2 bytes); the pipeline also needs a 22.72 GB UMT5-XXL text encoder and a 3.09 GB Whisper-Large audio encoder that the name does not mention
candidates.license: mit — and the foundation repo meituan-longcat/LongCat-Video it depends on is ALSO mit, and NEITHER is gated. The ComfyUI GGUF repack is mit too.

requirement.basis: THE GGUF/COMFYUI ROUTE IS PRICED HERE, NOT THE AUTHORS' ROUTE, because BeTenshi's video lane is ComfyUI and the repack is built for it. Disk is EXACT from repo listings read 02-11: vantagewithai/LongCat-Video-Avatar-1.5-GGUF-ComfyUI LongCat-Avatar-15_comfy-Q4_K_S.gguf 11,665,875,968 B + this repo's whisper-large-v3/model.safetensors 3,087,130,976 B + vocal_separator/Kim_Vocal_2.onnx 66,759,214 B + meituan-longcat/LongCat-Video vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors 507,591,892 B = 15,327,358,050 B. ONE REUSE IS ASSUMED AND MUST BE CHECKED BEFORE IT IS COUNTED AS FREE: the text encoder is google/umt5-xxl (confirmed from LongCat-Video/text_encoder/config.json, UMT5EncoderModel, 22.72 GB at fp32), which is the same encoder Wan 2.2 loads, and config/model-meta.json's basis for local-wan2.2-14b records 'the 6.7 GB text encoder' — the fp8-scaled UMT5-XXL ComfyUI uses. So the encoder is very probably already on D: and is excluded from diskGb; if it is not, add about 6.7 GB. VRAM 13.4 is the Q4_K_S DiT x 1.15 and is a WORKING-MINIMUM ADMISSION FIGURE in the same sense model-meta uses for every video alias on this box, NOT an empty-card peak — the 02-10 bake-off measured whole-card peaks of 28.0-30.1 GB for the three installed video models whose admission figures are 14-16 GB, so expect the same shape here. RAM 26 covers the 6.7 GB encoder, 3.09 GB Whisper, 0.51 GB VAE and ComfyUI's own working set with the same headroom model-meta gives local-hunyuanvideo-1.5 (24 GB). NOTHING HERE IS MEASURED ON EITHER BOX. For reference, the authors' own route is far more expensive: bf16 DiT 31.71 + dmd_lora 2.52 + whisper 3.09 + vocal separator 0.07 + fp32 UMT5-XXL 22.72 + VAE 0.51 = 60.62 GB, or 44.79 GB using the repo's own base_model_int8 (15.88 GB).

candidates.why: THE FIRST CANDIDATE THE `avatar` LANE HAS EVER HAD, and it is exactly the kind of thing docs/models.md added the lane to catch: the brief notes that 'whole capabilities (talking avatars, upscaling, live voice) shipped open weights without this report noticing', and this repo is five months old. It is trending now because of the ComfyUI GGUF repack, not because it is new. WHAT IT WOULD LET THE OWNER MAKE THAT NEITHER BOX CAN MAKE TODAY, which is the bar docs/models.md sets for an empty lane: a character who speaks. Both boxes can write a script, read it aloud (Chatterbox on :8004, Kokoro on :8002) and animate a still forward (Wan/LTX/Hunyuan in ComfyUI), and nothing joins those three — there is no path from an audio clip to a face whose mouth matches it. This model takes audio plus a still plus a prompt (AT2V, ATI2V and video continuation, single- or multi-stream audio) and holds identity across a long clip. AND IT LANDS ON A KNOWN PROBLEM RATHER THAN A HYPOTHETICAL ONE: docs/video-forge.md spends a whole section on continuity — characters redrawn from text every shot, a continuity-supervisor pass, first-frame cast checks, clips remade when they 'grow a person' — and the stated fix was character sheets plus hosted first frames. Audio-driven continuation with 'strict identity consistency' is the same problem attacked from the other end. WHY IT IS CHEAP HERE SPECIFICALLY: two of its three components are already on BeTenshi in some form. The audio encoder is Whisper-Large (the card says it replaced Wav2Vec2 with Whisper-Large for smoother lip dynamics) and the text encoder is UMT5-XXL, which is Wan 2.2's encoder — so the marginal download is the 11.67 GB Q4_K_S DiT plus a 3.09 GB HF Whisper checkpoint (BeTenshi's :8001 whisper is a CTranslate2 int8_float16 build at a self-reported 1.5 GB, so that one does NOT substitute) plus a 0.51 GB VAE. 15.33 GB for a capability, against 20.3 GB for the image service already running. LICENCE IS CLEAN ON ALL THREE REPOS: mit, not gated, on the avatar weights, on the LongCat-Video foundation repo its VAE and encoder come from, and on the GGUF repack. The card's own licence section says so in words: 'The model weights are released under the MIT License.' THIS IS A BETENSHI ENTRY. The authors' install needs torch cu124 and flash_attn 2.7.4.post1, which is CUDA, and B5 runs Draw Things rather than ComfyUI so the WanVideoWrapper route is not there either. NO `runtimes` PIN IS SET, deliberately and for the same reason as Iris-3B: GGUF and safetensors are portable formats and docs/models.md says runtimes must speak only where the FORMAT pins the hardware. It is the sampler that is CUDA-only, and that belongs in prose. ADOPTION, by metric: 3,391 downloads in the last 30 days and 12,911 all-time on the weights; the GGUF repack is 25,257 and 90,600, so the ComfyUI route is where the users are. WHAT IS NOT KNOWN: nothing measures this. There is no avatar board, the only evaluation is the authors' own — 508 image-audio pairs, 770 crowdsourced raters, 13,240 judgements, 10 expert assessors over physical rationality, audio-visual harmony, temporal stability and identity consistency — reported as two figures in a PNG rather than as numbers, and benchmarked against unnamed 'leading commercial models'. So the ranking here is licence and adoption, per docs/models.md clause 5b, and no quality claim is made.

Host RAM is the server process only: at 6.76 GB the weight set fits BeTenshi's card outright, so unlike the image models it needs no CPU offload and holds no standing host-RAM cost. BENCHMARK PROVENANCE AND A CHANGE IN IT THAT MATTERS: the board's results dataset still returns 401, so these come from the Space's own _refresh_leaderboard endpoint (https://hf-audio-open-tts-leaderboard.hf.space, build 'Last updated on 30 October 2026'). candidates.why: STILL THE SECOND CLONING VOICE, AND THE LANE DID NOT MOVE — which is worth stating plainly because the board's headline numbers all changed and that is a dataset change, not a model change. ON CV3-EVAL ENGLISH IN CLONING MODE, the one dataset and language where this model and the service on :8004 are both scored, AuK-Flash is 2.30 WER / 72.67 SIM / 26.61 RTFx against ChatterboxMultilingualTTS's 3.42 / 53.13 / 0.99 — identical to three decimals to what the 26-10 report published, re-pulled rather than carried. So 33% lower word error, +19.54 speaker-similarity points on the one axis a cloning service exists for, and 27x the throughput, under the same MIT licence. local-chatterbox IS the Multilingual variant per config/model-meta.json, so that is the right comparison and not the English-only ChatterboxTTS sibling. A CORRECTION TO THE 26-10 ENTRY, IN THE OPEN: it said the 21-10 build's new UTMOS metric put AuK-Flash at 'bottom of the cloning board' at 3.60. That was wrong, and it is wrong on the current build too. On CV3-Eval English cloning, AuK-Flash's 3.60 is above ydqmkkx/GibbsTTS 3.25, IndexTeam/IndexTTS-2.5 3.37, openbmb/VoxCPM2 3.40, vibevoice/VibeVoice-7B-hf 3.40, vibevoice/VibeVoice-1.5B-hf 3.42, maya-research/maya2-native 3.45 and its own tencent/AuK sibling 3.53 — seventh from the bottom of twenty-three, not last. On the all-datasets default mix it reads 3.90 and is mid-table. THE UNDERLYING POINT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION and is why it is kept rather than deleted: UTMOS is a predicted naturalness score, Chatterbox has no UTMOS figure at all on the cloning board, so this is NOT a comparison with the running service — it is a reason to listen to output before committing a service. SIM IS WHERE IT WINS AND IT STILL WINS OUTRIGHT AMONG CLEAN LICENCES: AuK 73.00 and AuK-Flash 72.67 are the top two SIM scores on the board, ahead of OmniVoice 70.05 (non-commercial), VoxCPM2 69.02 and Qwen3-TTS-Base 66.96; the one new arrival on this axis, GibbsTTS, is 66.75 under MIT at a third the size and 5.92 SIM points behind. Take Flash and not the base: same 6.76 GB, 0.14 WER worse, 6x the speed. THE COST, unchanged: AuK-Flash declares zh and en only, where Chatterbox declares 23 including Arabic, and no board measures Arabic at all. So this is an ADDITION for English and Chinese, not a repoint of :8004 — and a new service to write, because AuK is an instruction-driven pipeline that also does speech editing, enhancement and source separation, which nothing on either box can do. On BeTenshi 6.76 GB sits on the card beside Kokoro's 0.4 GB and Chatterbox's measured 3.0 GB without disturbing either; unremarkable on B5. ADOPTION IS STILL FALLING AND THAT IS STILL A FACT AGAINST IT: 845 downloads in the last 30 days against 1,073 a week ago and 2,963 a fortnight before that, 4,153 all-time.
